slides.say: A suitcase lock has three wheels. Each wheel shows one of the digits one to nine, and no digit may appear twice. How many codes are possible?
at: A suitcase lock has three wheels

slides.say: It's the same lock as in the last question, with one change. Now no digit may appear twice.
Let's solve it the math way, in stages. This time it's without repetition.
The first wheel has nine options. Say we pick four.
Now the four leaves the pool. It can't come back, because no digit may appear twice.
So the second wheel has only eight options left.
Two digits are used now, so the third wheel has seven options.
Then seventy-two times seven. Seventy times seven is four hundred ninety. And two times seven is fourteen.
Four hundred ninety plus fourteen is five hundred four.
Compare with the last question. The same digits, but the pool shrinks after every pick. Nine, nine, nine became nine, eight, seven.
And careful, we don't divide by anything here. One two three and two one three are different codes. Dividing by six gives eighty-four, choice number two, and that's a trap.
at: One two three and two one three

slides.say: Choice number four is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number four is our answer
